cells.tense: You can see the whole shape of what you carried, and you are not looking away from it.
cells.ask: Name one finished thing to somebody today, plainly, or write it down and leave it where you will pass tomorrow.
cells.core:
You can hold the entire picture at once — what went in, what came out, who it was for. Standing back from it like this is not the same as leaving it. You are in the room and you can still see the whole room.

The way you tend this is steady. Care that doesn't exhaust itself, a hand that stays open instead of closing around the thing. Nothing is being forced and nothing is being dropped. That's the balance: attention that keeps its footing. The risk in it is small and worth knowing — with the whole shape in view, the finished part can slide past unmarked. Say the one thing that ended. Then pick up what's next when it arrives.

cells.verb: letting what was given be seen and counted
cells.place: a vantage where the whole shape of it is visible at once

cells.tense: Some part of you is already standing where the answer comes down, waiting on a door that hasn't opened.
cells.ask: Take one thing that's already done and leave it alone for a week — no polishing, no re-checking, no watching for a reaction.
cells.core:
You are ahead of the moment. The work isn't finished and you are already rehearsing how it will land — whether the effort gets counted, whether the thing registers, what it will mean once it does. The waiting started before there was anything to wait for.

You can read the pattern perfectly, and the reading has turned into an argument for why it ought to be valued. That argument costs the hours the work needs, and it doesn't arrive at an answer — it just runs. Nothing about the case changes whether anyone actually notices.

The way back is small. Let one finished thing stay finished. The practice is to stop where the thing ends.

cells.tense: You've stopped standing where the finished thing can be seen, and you're still doing the work from back here.
cells.ask: Do one small physical task you've been putting off — fix it, sort it, mend it, close it — in one sitting, with no one watching.
cells.core:
You can read the whole pattern when you let yourself. What got built, what it took, who it reached. The reading is there.

The offering has gone quiet. The work still gets done, and the moment where it would be handed over and acknowledged stopped happening somewhere. So you carry the weight and skip the count. Full hands, no record of what left them.

The ground back is concrete. Put your hands on something small and finish it. Not for anyone. Just to feel the end of a thing land in the room, where you can stand next to it. Then there's something solid to hand over later, if handing over seems worth doing again. Start with the small close.

cells.tense: You're keeping the account of what each thing cost, and you talk about that accounting as though it runs itself.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you gave up that nobody asked you to give up — no explanation after it, no softening.
cells.core:
You know what things cost. What was spent, what it bought, what's still owed. That knowing is real and it's working — you can read the whole shape of a situation faster than most people can read part of it.

What isn't claimed is the counting itself. You describe the account as a fact about your circumstances rather than something you sit down and do. So the person doing the arithmetic goes unnamed, and what you handed over can't be a gift — it's just how things are. That's the mislabel, and it's the whole of it.

Say one item out loud, once, without the explanation. It doesn't have to be owed to anyone. It only has to be said by the one who kept the count.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the count. Call it yours once.
